The call was contained in a statement dated November 22, 2026, condemning the alleged incident, which reportedly occurred on November 14.
The statement described the allegations against the 92-year-old monarch as disturbing, urging the Katsina State Government and the Nigeria Police Force to ensure that the matter is thoroughly investigated.
It alleged that videos shared on social media by the tourist showed the emir making inappropriate advances towards her despite her resistance.
The statement further condemned what it described as predatory behaviour, insisting that the allegations should not be ignored because of the monarch’s position.
It called for a transparent and independent investigation, stressing that the emir should be held accountable if found culpable.
The statement also urged that any prosecution should follow due process and a fair trial, without recourse to the death penalty.
It added that the incident presented an opportunity for the Nigerian government to demonstrate that nobody was above the law.
The statement further linked the allegations to what it described as the normalisation of rape and sexual violence in the country, arguing that such offences were often committed with impunity.
